subject: Decision: Hosted vs Dedicated – Latency/Throughput follow-up

Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Decision: Hosted vs Dedicated – Latency/Throughput follow-up

Thanks again for taking time today, Alex & Sophie – good conversation. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Summary from the call: FinPay is evaluating Redwood to power high-throughput, low-latency inference for live payment fraud scoring. You indicated a target of ~200 requests/sec with ~20 tokens per request and a p95 latency target of ~50ms.
- Key tradeoff: Hosted API gives fastest time-to-value; Dedicated provides predictable throughput, lower tail latencies, and stronger isolation (recommended if you need sustained p95 <100ms at 200 rps).

Attachments: redwood_mutual_action_plan.pdf (MTP), I've also included an internal latency/throughput benchmark we use for configs.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Can you confirm the 200 rps / 20 tokens / 50ms p95 numbers?
2) If confirmed, we recommend a 2-week Dedicated pilot (reserved capacity) to validate p95 under your real traffic shape. I attached a mutual action plan with milestones and dates.
3) We can prepare a formal pilot quote (hardware + support) once you confirm the numbers.

If you'd prefer, Neha (cc'd) can follow up with suggested Dedicated sizing and expected p95 numbers based on our benchmarks.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Schedule time: https://calendly.com/dylan-brooks/30min

Subject: Re: Decision: Hosted vs Dedicated – Latency/Throughput follow-up

Thanks Dylan – helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications: 

- The 200 rps is our steady-state target for the fraud scoring endpoint (peak bursts up to ~300 rps for ~30s).
- Average request size is ~18 tokens; 95th token size maybe ~30 tokens for some edge cases.
- The 50ms p95 is aggressive but what our product team wants for the inline flow. Realistic window is 50–100ms.

Two questions for Neha: 
1) How does Dedicated handle the short bursts to 300 rps – will we see p95 degradation during burst windows?
2) Does Redwood pre-warm or keep GPUs hot to avoid cold-starts, or would we need to allocate buffer capacity?

If Dedicated will keep p95 close to 50–100ms in the scenarios above, we're likely to proceed with a pilot.

Alex Moreno
Head of Engineering, FinPay

Subject: Re: Decision: Hosted vs Dedicated – Latency/Throughput follow-up (technical follow-up)

Hi Alex / Sophie – looping in technical details and expected numbers based on the traffic profile you shared. Short answer: Dedicated is the right starting point for inline 50–100ms p95 at sustained 200 rps with 300 rps short bursts. Below are specifics and what we recommend for a pilot.

What Dedicated gives you: 
- Reserved capacity (no noisy neighbors) and predictable batching behavior – we can pin a pool to your account so runtime does not multiplex with other customers.
- Pre-warm and pinned workers: we advise keeping a minimum worker count to avoid cold-starts; Dedicated supports instant routing to hot workers.
- Autoscaling + burst buffer: we can configure a modest burst buffer to handle 300 rps short bursts without impacting p95.

Benchmarks / expected latency (approx, based on our internal runtimes and the model family you mentioned):
- Config: 2 x A100-equivalent workers (or equivalent vGPUs) with optimized kernels, per-worker throughput ~120 rps at ~20 tokens with p95 ~40–60ms when pinned and warmed.
- Cluster-level: with 2 workers and a lightweight request router we can sustain ~200 rps p95 in the 50–80ms ballpark; adding a 3rd worker raises headroom for 300 rps bursts and reduces p95 variance.
- Batching: continuous batching provides efficiency; we tune batching latency cap to keep p95 within your 50–100ms SLO.

Pilot recommendation (2 weeks):
1) Dedicated pool: start with 2 workers, policy: minimum hot_workers=2, burst_capacity=1 worker for short spikes.
2) Observability: enable token-level latency breakdowns and per-route p95 dashboards (we'll share dashboards).
3) Run your real request trace (or replay a sample) during pilot. We'll run a stress test that simulates 200 rps steady + 300 rps bursts to validate p95.

Notes: 
- Hosted API could meet your needs for non-inline / async batch scoring or for quick PoC, but it will be harder to hit sustained low-tail p95 for inline production at 200 rps.
- We will provide a formal pilot quote (hardware + support + observability) and a mutual action plan for signoffs.

I'm attaching our runtime latency/throughput benchmark summary for similar customers. Link to full benchmark sheet: https://redwood.box.com/s/benchmarks-2027-04

Let me know if you'd like us to size a 3-worker pilot upfront (recommended if you want comfortable headroom during business-hours peaks).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
